If template holes are unregistered, yaw alone does not register them; use observed features or explicit ordinary placement with alignHoles=false and offset.

flip.description: place: turn the held object upside down before setting it down. pick: take it so that it can be turned over later; some arms take it tilted for that, and a place with flip says when the object must be picked again with flip.

roll.description: place: tip the held object about the arm before setting it down, radians (π/2 = 90° onto its side). Not together with flip.

clearance.description: place, pour: least gap in metres kept to objects already on the surface (default 0.015). With an offset, 0 allows contact or overlap (interlocking pieces, stacking): the spot is used exactly as requested, never shifted aside. Screw-hole alignment always uses 0.

tools.name: ego_inspect
tools.description: Look closely at the top face of an object with one fresh frame of each camera, read from the camera that sees most of it: its colours on a px x px grid. rows is in the object's own frame (row 0 is its +y edge, column 0 its -x edge, as seen from above with its heading yawDeg). worldRows is the same face as seen from above with the map's +y up and +x to the right: rows turned worldTurnDeg counter-clockwise (yawDeg rounded to a quarter turn), so faces of objects lying at different headings compare directly in worldRows. Putting an object down with place yaw = its current yawDeg + k x 90 degrees (given in radians) turns its face k quarter turns counter-clockwise as seen from above. Each cell is [r, g, b] or null where the face is out of view or hidden. Stand within about a metre with the object in front of you. You have two cameras on your head: head_camera looks ahead and sees a surface only from some way ahead of it; wide_camera, a short-focal-length camera tilted further down, also sees the strip of a table next to the edge you stand at and the gripper at work, in less detail. When part of the face is unseen, hint says why (too close below the view, beside or behind it, too far, hidden) and how to move. Use it to compare printed or patterned faces, read which side of a flat object is up, or tell similar objects apart. A printed flat object lying with its plain back up: use plain === true or interiorColors (under about 20). Do not use spread / interiorSpread alone — table lighting makes cardboard look variegated in RGB even when it is one colour. Turn it over (place with flip) and look again. Flat objects lying on or against each other hide parts of their faces and can be perceived as one object, and one lying on another can hide it wholly: set them apart on free space first, looking again where each one lay after picking it up. The object frame stays fixed to the object between views and while it is carried, so one inspection before picking it tells which place yaw turns its face as you want.

entity.description: Id of the object to inspect.

px.description: Grid size, 4 to 128 (default 24). Raise it when sourcePx is large and you need pattern detail.

tools.name: ego_match_face
tools.description: Find where the top faces of objects appear on the top face of a reference object printed at the same scale (puzzle pieces on the picture of their box, tiles on a pattern sheet). It works from the faces you remember: the robot remembers the top face of every object up to about 0.6 m that it sees within 1.5 m (ego_state appearance says how much and how long ago), and refreshes the ones in view first; a face put down since it was last seen must be looked at again. Match all objects of a task in one call. For each it compares the colours of every placement and quarter turn and returns the best few: offsetM is where the face centre belongs on the reference, in the reference frame from its centre; turnDeg is how far the face must turn counter-clockwise to line up with the reference; placeYawDeg is the heading (degrees; place takes radians) that lines it up with the reference as the reference lies now. To build the picture elsewhere at heading H, put each object at centre + offsetM turned by H, with place yaw = H + turnDeg. score is a correlation (1 = identical); a best score barely above the second is ambiguous, so look closer (raise px toward 32) and match again. offsetM is good to about one cell (cellM): when you know the layout (for example a grid of equal pieces), snap it to the nearest slot. plain / interiorColors (under about 20) means a cardboard back facing up; do not trust spread alone. An entry with error says what to look at.

entities.description: Ids of the objects whose faces are sought.

reference.description: Id of the object showing the whole picture.

px.description: Cells across each object's shorter side, 4 to 32 (default 24).

tools.name: ego_annotate
tools.description: Record what you have identified an object to be when the perceived category is wrong or unknown (for example "unknown" for a box or a puzzle piece). Your label replaces its category, and the affordances you name replace the category's defaults, so prediction and planning treat it accordingly: graspable (can be picked), support-surface (things can be put on it), receptacle (things can be put in it), container, pourable (can be carried with its contents and poured), flat.

label.description: Category name to use for it.

tools.name: ego_forget
tools.description: Remove an object from the Ego State as a false perception. Use it only for an object that is physically implausible (marked `unsupported`: floating with nothing under it, or inside another solid object) and that you looked for again, with ego_observe from a place where its spot is in view, without perceiving it (its lastSeenAgoS keeps growing). The robot refuses an object it holds or perceived in the last few seconds.

reason.description: Why it is implausible and how you looked for it again.

tools.name: ego_candidates
tools.description: Find the objects that could be what the instruction calls something when perception names it differently: the segmenter names things by appearance (a lid printed with a picture can be "picture"), and the classifier only knows the shapes of its categories. Ranks objects by how well their perceived category alternatives, segmenter names and size fit `name` and `size`; without either, lists the objects whose current name is doubtful. Each carries `doubts` and the evidence behind its name. Confirm with ego_inspect or a closer look, then ego_annotate.

name.description: What you are looking for, as a category word, for example "box" or "lid".

size.description: One to three approximate dimensions in metres from the instruction or your expectation.

tools.name: skill_run
tools.description: Execute the plan of a receipt from ego_predict. Waits for the skill to finish unless wait is false. Staged assembly skills can take tens of minutes: a wait timeout leaves the job running. Poll its status; keep each run_code wait at most 240 seconds and do not body_stop just because a poll times out. The robot refuses receipts that are infeasible, expired, already used, or above the risk limit.

tools.name: skill_status
tools.description: Read the state of a running or finished skill.

tools.name: body_stop
tools.description: Stop all motion immediately and hold the current pose.

tools.name: report_problem
tools.description: Alert the operator that you hit a situation you cannot resolve by yourself: an unexpected error, a skill that keeps failing, or a task that cannot be done from here. Before calling, review your own tool calls in this turn and diagnose: which prediction or skill failed, the error text, how often it repeated, where you were, and how it relates to blockers, uncertainty, or missing or duplicate objects in the ego state. The operator console shows the report as an alert. Report once per unresolved issue. Recoverable skill failures with a nextAction should first follow that recovery using fresh perception; do not end the task solely because a landing is unknown or one component is finished. Stop only when further progress actually requires operator intervention.

goal.description: What you are trying to achieve.

step.description: The step you were carrying out when you got stuck.

diagnosis.description: The cause you diagnosed from your tool log and the evidence for it.

message.description: What happened, what you tried, and what you need from the operator.

programQuestions: 一、错误：程序哪里写错了（语法、变量重复声明、未定义的名字、类型不符）？
二、修正：怎样改写后重试；不要原样再提交同一段代码。
若提示同名变量已声明：执行环境会保留顶层绑定；把本次临时声明放在 { ... } 块内，或使用新名字。不要用 var 重声明已有 const/let；也不要给 const 重新赋值。解释后继续调用 run_code 执行修正。

extraTools.name: capability_list
extraTools.description: List the capabilities you saved in earlier tasks, without their code: programs you wrote that combine the robot tools to do something no single tool does. Check it before writing a new program; a capability that fits saves you from solving the problem again. Each has a layer (recipe: skills composed for one kind of task; skill: one reusable operation), a status (verified: it succeeded in several runs; candidate: not yet proven; deprecated: it kept failing, fix it or delete it), what it requires and ensures, and the outcomes of its runs. Verified ones come first, recipes before skills.

extraTools.name: capability_get
extraTools.description: Fetch a saved capability, including its code. Run it inside run_code: `const cap = await tools.capability_get({ name }); const run = new (Object.getPrototypeOf(async function () {}).constructor)("tools", "args", cap.code); return await run(tools, { ...arguments })`. The program that fetched it counts as one run of it: succeeded when the program ends without an error, failed when it throws.

extraTools.name: capability_save
extraTools.description: Save a program as a named capability of this robot so later tasks can reuse it, or replace an existing one with an improved version (changed code starts a new version as a candidate). Save it after it has worked. Prefer small skills that work on any objects of a kind (spread objects out, turn a flat object face up, find where a piece belongs in a picture, lay objects out on a grid), and a thin recipe that composes them with capability_get. Write the code as the body of an async function of (tools, args) that calls the same tools as your run_code programs, returns its result and throws an Error when it cannot achieve what it ensures. Everything specific to one task belongs in args: saving is refused when the code names objects (e:123) or holds many decimal constants.

layer.description: skill: one reusable operation; recipe: skills composed for one kind of task.

description.description: What it does and what it returns.

requires.description: What must hold in the world before it runs.

ensures.description: What holds in the world after it succeeded.

parameters.description: What each field of args means, for example {"lid": "id of the lid showing the picture"}.

code.description: Body of an async function of (tools, args).

extraTools.name: capability_delete
extraTools.description: Forget a capability that is wrong, superseded by a better or more general one, or no longer useful: it leaves the list and can no longer be fetched. Merge near-duplicates into one capability and delete the rest.

reason.description: Why it is forgotten, for example "superseded by lay_out_on_grid".

extraTools.name: reflect
extraTools.description: Reflect before trying again when the task is not progressing although no tool failed: a result does not match the goal, something expected is missing, or the same approach keeps falling short. Describe the difficulty; returns the operator's messages, earlier failures, the robot's evidence on the objects involved and, for a deep reflection, a digest of the scene, then the questions to answer before the next step. Print the returned text and answer it after the program ends.

difficulty.description: What is going wrong, with the observations that show it.

name.description: The object the instruction means, as a category word, when one is involved.

size.description: Its approximate dimensions in metres, if known.

depth.description: shallow: a quick check of one step; deep (default): question the understanding of the task, the assumptions and the method.

extraTools.name: rgbd_video_gen_capabilities
extraTools.description: Read rgbd_video_gen readiness, current defaults and limits. Does not run generation.

extraTools.name: rgbd_video_gen_prepare_scene
extraTools.description: Build and save a SINGLE-TIMESTAMP snapshot scene from ego_capture_cameras capture.json. For whole-motion evidence use prepare_recording instead. Defaults to ONLY the middle head_camera RGB; explicitly select other source_cameras when requested. Targets are virtual OpenCV cameras described by a rigid camera_to_frame matrix OR position/look_at/up vectors. frame=reference uses the captured middle camera axes (right/down/forward); frame=gripper uses the synchronized gripper axes (forward/left/up). All positions are metres. Gripper-forward example: frame=gripper, position=[0,0,0], look_at=[1,0,0], up=[0,0,1]. No target is chosen implicitly. Reuses middle-camera intrinsics. Submit the returned scene_path with its exact num_source_views and max_target_views. No shell, file-authoring tools, subagents or remote generation are needed for preparation.

source_cameras.description: Unique evidence camera IDs in order. Default [head_camera]; use side cameras only when explicitly requested.

targets.description: 1-24 virtual cameras. For each supply a matrix OR all three look-at vectors, never both.

position.description: Camera centre [x,y,z] in the selected frame, metres.

look_at.description: Point [x,y,z] to look toward, in the selected frame, metres.

up.description: Image-up direction [x,y,z] in the selected frame; nonparallel to viewing direction.

label.description: Optional target label retained in scene metadata.

extraTools.name: rgbd_video_gen_prepare_recording
extraTools.description: Prepare a scene from a succeeded ego_rgb_recording, retaining ALL recorded middle head_camera RGB images and measured poses locally. Use for evidence captured throughout motion; never replace it with the final ego_capture_cameras snapshot. Selected source images are timestamped views from the same camera in one measured frame. Targets use the same explicit matrix/look-at descriptions as prepare_scene; frame=reference is the FIRST recorded middle OpenCV camera, frame=gripper is the CURRENT gripper. The remote API declares at most 8 source views per job. Omit selection to use all if at most 8, otherwise uniformly sample 8 across the full recording including both endpoints. Optional num_source_views overrides the uniform sample count; source_frame_indices selects chronological indices for subsets/batches. Never claim all images conditioned the model when only a subset was used. Returns selected indices, all_frames_used, full recording_manifest_path and exact submission counts; no navigation or remote inference.

num_source_views.description: Optional 1-8 uniformly spaced temporal views; default min(8, recorded_frames). Includes route endpoints when count is at least 2. Exclusive with source_frame_indices.

source_frame_indices.description: Optional 1-8 distinct increasing recorded frame indices, for explicit subsets or batches. Exclusive with count.

targets.description: 1-24 virtual cameras. For each supply a matrix OR all three look-at vectors, never both.

position.description: Camera centre [x,y,z] in the selected frame, metres.

look_at.description: Point [x,y,z] to look toward, in the selected frame, metres.

up.description: Image-up direction [x,y,z] in the selected frame; nonparallel to viewing direction.

label.description: Optional target label retained in scene metadata.

extraTools.name: rgbd_video_gen_submit
extraTools.description: Upload a local rgbd_videogen_scene_v1 JSON scene with inline PNG/JPEG base64 images. Requires 2-64 ordered frames and at least num_source_views + 1 frames, known intrinsics and OpenCV camera-to-world poses in metres. First num_source_views frames provide evidence; remaining frames are target poses with optional images for GT comparison. Returns an accepted job, not completion. This sends images to the configured remote server. It does not estimate poses or accept SLARM capture ZIPs.

scene_path.description: JSON file beneath inputRoot; relative paths resolve from that root.

request_key.description: Stable operation key: 8-128 letters/digits or ._:-. Reuse exactly after disconnects or unknown outcomes; new keys create new work.

num_source_views.description: First 1-8 frames are evidence images; omitted uses current server default (normally 6). Explicitly set for fewer than 6 evidence images, e.g. 3 for a three-camera snapshot plus target poses. The model was trained on 6 evidence views; other counts may reduce quality.

max_target_views.description: Target view limit, 1-24; omitted uses server default.

num_inference_steps.description: Euler sampling steps, 1-100; omitted uses server default.

seed.description: Nonnegative integer random seed; omitted uses server default.

output_fps.description: Output video fps, 1-60; omitted uses server default.

extraTools.name: rgbd_video_gen_upload
extraTools.description: Upload a local ZIP containing rgbd_videogen_scene_v1 scene.json and its relative image files. Uses server generation defaults. Not compatible with world_capture slarm_scene_v1 ZIPs. Returns job_id; use status then result and download.

archive_path.description: ZIP beneath inputRoot, at most the configured upload limit.

request_key.description: Stable operation key: 8-128 letters/digits or ._:-. Reuse exactly after disconnects or unknown outcomes; new keys create new work.

extraTools.name: rgbd_video_gen_demo
extraTools.description: Generate from a named server-installed demo, e.g. waymo080 or re10k_172c99489b18e0e6. No local images are needed. trajectory uses its target camera path; bev generates bird-eye poses and has no target ground truth. With bev, explicitly provide num_bev_views and bev_altitude_scale.

request_key.description: Stable operation key: 8-128 letters/digits or ._:-. Reuse exactly after disconnects or unknown outcomes; new keys create new work.

num_source_views.description: First 1-8 frames are evidence images; omitted uses current server default (normally 6). Explicitly set for fewer than 6 evidence images, e.g. 3 for a three-camera snapshot plus target poses. The model was trained on 6 evidence views; other counts may reduce quality.

max_target_views.description: Target view limit, 1-24; omitted uses server default.

num_inference_steps.description: Euler sampling steps, 1-100; omitted uses server default.

seed.description: Nonnegative integer random seed; omitted uses server default.

output_fps.description: Output video fps, 1-60; omitted uses server default.

bev_altitude_scale.description: Required for bev: positive height multiplier of the source camera horizontal radius.

extraTools.name: rgbd_video_gen_status
extraTools.description: Query generation. queued/running are pending; succeeded requires result; failed/cancelled means stop and report error. 100% progress alone is not success.

job_id.description: Actual j_ job_id returned by rgbd_video_gen. Never invent ids.

wait_seconds.description: Bounded wait in seconds, default 0 (one query); provider limit defaults to 20. Aborting polling does not cancel generation.

extraTools.name: rgbd_video_gen_result
extraTools.description: Read a successful result and save its manifest. RGB, metric depth and videos are predictions, not observed geometry. Target PSNR exists only with target GT. target_cameras[i] maps to pred_{num_source_views+i}.jpg, not always pred_{6+i}.jpg. Select remote filenames for download; local_filename distinguishes source_reconstruction_*.jpg from target_prediction_*.jpg.

job_id.description: Actual j_ job_id returned by rgbd_video_gen. Never invent ids.

extraTools.name: rgbd_video_gen_download
extraTools.description: Save under outputsDir and return local_manifest_path for downstream consumers. Download exact artifact filenames from a successful result (videos, frames.zip, depth.npz, comparison strip, meta.json). Saves loose predictions as source_reconstruction_*.jpg or zero-based target_prediction_*.jpg; ZIP entries retain remote names. Verifies byte counts and SHA256 before publishing local files; retries reuse verified files. No arbitrary URL or destination path is accepted.

job_id.description: Actual j_ job_id returned by rgbd_video_gen. Never invent ids.

extraTools.name: rgbd_video_gen_cancel
extraTools.description: Explicitly cancel a job submitted or recovered in this local store. Stopping a chat does not cancel accepted remote work. Only cancelled=true confirms cancellation.

job_id.description: Actual j_ job_id returned by rgbd_video_gen. Never invent ids.

wait_seconds.description: Bounded wait in seconds, default 0 (one query); provider limit defaults to 20. Aborting polling does not cancel generation.

extraTools.name: novelanything_health
extraTools.description: Check hosted NovelAnything model readiness without inference.

extraTools.name: novelanything_samples
extraTools.description: List server demo samples or inspect one before selecting frames. Samples are not observations of robot surroundings.

sample_id.description: Omit to list samples; otherwise use an actual listed sample id.

extraTools.name: novelanything_upload
extraTools.description: Archive and upload a robot-workspace ZIP with root scene.json and posed RGB files, without inference. Robot RGB inputs must come only from the middle head_camera; depth inputs are unsupported by this skill; exclude head_camera_left and head_camera_right. Context needs RGB, OpenCV world-to-camera w2c and fxfycxcy; omit depth_path. Targets need w2c; no depth input or GT is used. A single capture or SLARM/rgbd_video_gen ZIP is not this format.

archive_path.description: Existing compliant scene ZIP beneath robot inputRoot.

request_key.description: Stable local request identity, 8–128 letters/digits or ._:-. Reuse after accepted replies. UNKNOWN_OUTCOME requires operator reconciliation; never retry with a new key.

extraTools.name: novelanything_prepare_gripper_view
extraTools.description: Prepare a local NovelAnything ZIP from a succeeded ego_rgb_recording. Uses only recorded middle head_camera RGB, with no depth input, and derives shared-frame w2c from synchronized robot odometry, encoders and the robot model. The target is the CURRENT gripper link origin looking along gripper +X with image-up +Z, using middle-camera intrinsics. Returns archive_path and context/target indices; retains all sampled evidence in the ZIP. No navigation, general shell/files or inference. Upload the returned archive with novelanything_upload, then submit with returned indices and label the result gripper_view_prediction. If preparation is unavailable or fails, report that failure; never substitute rgbd_video_gen for an explicitly requested NovelAnything job.

num_source_views.description: Optional 2–16 contexts, at most recorded frames; omitted selects up to 16 across the recording.

extraTools.name: novelanything_submit
extraTools.description: Queue NovelAnything RGB/depth prediction from exactly one sample_id or upload_id. When the user explicitly requests NovelAnything, do not substitute rgbd_video_gen if preparation or submission fails. Set both context and target or neither (scene defaults). Context: 2–16 distinct indices with RGB and calibration; target: 1–6 distinct disjoint indices. For robot evidence, all context frames must be from the same middle head_camera at different timestamps/poses; never combine side-camera RGB or supply depth. Targets may omit GT. Returns acceptance, not completion. No automatic POST retry; UNKNOWN_OUTCOME must be reconciled by the operator.

sample_id.description: Explicit demo sample id; mutually exclusive with upload_id.

upload_id.description: Id returned by novelanything_upload; mutually exclusive with sample_id.

context.description: Zero-based context frame indices; omit with target for scene defaults.

target.description: Zero-based target frame indices, disjoint from context.

metrics.description: Default true: score only targets with GT of that modality. False disables scoring, not prediction.

request_key.description: Stable local request identity, 8–128 letters/digits or ._:-. Reuse after accepted replies. UNKNOWN_OUTCOME requires operator reconciliation; never retry with a new key.

extraTools.name: novelanything_status
extraTools.description: Inspect or briefly poll a NovelAnything job. queued/running are pending; failed/cancelled/interrupted stop synthesis. Local timeout does not cancel remote work.

job_id.description: Exact job id returned by NovelAnything; never invent identities.

wait_seconds.description: Default 0: one query. Otherwise bounded by provider maxWaitSeconds (default 20).

extraTools.name: novelanything_result
extraTools.description: Read successful result metadata and exact artifact paths. Rejects every state except succeeded. Generated RGB and depth are predictions, not observations or motion clearance.

job_id.description: Exact job id returned by NovelAnything; never invent identities.

extraTools.name: novelanything_log
extraTools.description: Read bounded NovelAnything server job log for failure diagnosis.

job_id.description: Exact job id returned by NovelAnything; never invent identities.

extraTools.name: novelanything_download
extraTools.description: Download exact artifact paths from a successful result into outputs/novelanything/<job_id>, preserving subdirectories. Returns absolute files and local_manifest_path. Local SHA256 is recorded; server checksum verification occurs only when the server supplies a checksum.

job_id.description: Exact job id returned by NovelAnything; never invent identities.

artifact_paths.description: Unique nonempty selection of exact result.artifacts[].path values.

worldTools.name: world_status
worldTools.description: Read the loaded scenario, simulation time and speed, entities, robots (what they hold) and recent world events such as grasps.

worldTools.name: world_scene
worldTools.description: Read the true current World State: every entity with its exact pose and the relations between entities (what rests on what, what is held). This is ground truth that robots cannot see.

detail.description: Return the full SceneState instead of a compact listing (default false).

worldTools.name: asset_search
worldTools.description: List published assets, optionally filtered by a name/category substring or an exact category.

query.description: Substring of the asset name or category.

worldTools.name: asset_get
worldTools.description: Read one published asset, including its entity template and validation report.

worldTools.name: asset_create
worldTools.description: Create a draft asset and validate it physically (compiles, has mass, rests without tipping or sinking when dropped). Give either a generator with params (generators: building {width, depth, height}, counter {width, depth, height}, dining_table {width, depth, height, mass}, cabinet_with_drawer {width, depth, height, drawer_height}, cup {radius, height, mass, fragile}, plate, bowl, steward_bot) or an authored template. An entity template is a World State Entity with id "w:template" and an identity pose: {id, role: environment|object|robot|actor, category: {value}, pose: {value: {p: [0,0,0], q: [1,0,0,0]}}, body: {kind: "rigid", root: {value: fixed|planar|free}, links: [{id, name, geometry: {collision: [{kind: "primitive", shape: box|sphere|cylinder|capsule, size: full extents in metres (box [x,y,z], cylinder [r, length]), pose: {p, q}, rgba}], visual: [...]}, inertial: {value: {mass}}, material: {value: {friction, fragility}}, affordances: [{value: "graspable"}]}], joints: [{id, parent, child, type: {value: fixed|revolute|prismatic}, origin: {value: {p, q}}, axis: {value}, limits: {value: {lo, hi}}, q: {value: [0]}, qd: {value: [0]}}]}}. The origin sits on the floor at the footprint centre. Read an existing asset with asset_get for a full example. Nothing is published until asset_publish.

params.description: Generator parameters as a JSON object.

template.description: Authored entity template as a JSON object.

worldTools.name: asset_preview
worldTools.description: Render front and top preview images of a draft template and return the PNG file paths. Open the images with the file read tool to check the shape before publishing.

template.description: Entity template as a JSON object.

stem.description: File name stem for the images.

worldTools.name: asset_publish
worldTools.description: Validate and publish a template under a name. Publishing an identical template again keeps the same version.

template.description: Entity template as a JSON object.

meta.description: Free-form metadata object, for example the description it came from.

worldTools.name: scene_compose
worldTools.description: Compose a scene from published assets, check that nothing interpenetrates and that it settles, and save it. Spec: {name, entities: [{id: "w:<unique>", asset, at: {x, y, yaw}} or {id, asset, on: "w:<support id placed earlier>", offset: [dx, dy], yaw}], regions: [{id, label, polygon: [[x, y], ...]}]}. Place robots with at; place objects on furniture with on.

worldTools.name: scene_render
worldTools.description: Render overview images of a saved scene and return the PNG paths for the file read tool.

worldTools.name: scenario_save
worldTools.description: Save a scenario: {name, scene, robots: ["w:<robot id>"], task: "<instruction for the robots>"}. The task must not reveal ground truth the robots should discover themselves.

worldTools.name: world_catalog
worldTools.description: List saved scenes and scenarios.

worldTools.name: episode_control
worldTools.description: Load a saved scenario as the running episode (robots get fresh bodies and ports), or reset the current episode to its initial state.

worldTools.name: world_clock
worldTools.description: Pause or resume the simulation, or set its speed factor.

value.description: Speed factor for speed, for example 2.

worldTools.name: world_edit
worldTools.description: Change the running World State without stopping the episode (robots keep working and must notice the change themselves). move: relocate an object or piece of furniture; objects resting on moved furniture move with it. spawn: add a new entity from a published asset (see asset_search). remove: delete an entity; objects resting on it fall. Place with x/y (floor position in metres, world frame) or with on (support entity id, e.g. "w:table") plus offset_x/offset_y in the support frame. yaw in radians; move keeps the current yaw when omitted. Robots, the building and objects a robot is holding cannot be edited; an edit that would interpenetrate another entity is rejected and leaves the world unchanged. Read world_scene first for ids and positions.

entity.description: Entity id, e.g. "w:cup-1"; for spawn a new unique id.

asset.description: Published asset name for spawn, e.g. "cup".

on.description: Support entity id to place on, e.g. "w:sideboard".

offset_x.description: x offset on the support, in the support frame (default 0).

offset_y.description: y offset on the support, in the support frame (default 0).

worldTools.name: observer_report
worldTools.description: Read how accurate each robot's own world model is compared with the true World State: object recall, false detections, position error, uncertainty calibration (NEES) and self-localisation error.
